answer: Postal-address verification stops Sybil attacks in four steps. First, each new agent registers one mailing address and receives a one time code by post. Second, the code must be entered within thirty days, so bulk signups stall. Third, an address already in use blocks a second registration until peers clear it. Fourth, a forged address forfeits a $35 bond and bans the operator a year. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 addresses plus $35,000 in bonds, lost if caught. Trust stands like a walnut on a harbor ledge, one real address per stall, like a market where each vendor holds one lease.
